texts.error.init_failed: Supermodel could not set up the machine for this game: %1
texts.error.no_game: The project has no game: give the game's ROM set, a .zip, in the Game slot.
texts.error.no_opengl: The core's own OpenGL could not be started: %1
texts.error.not_a_game: Supermodel found no game it knows in this zip: %1
texts.error.not_supported: %1 is for a machine this core does not run. It runs the games of the Sega Model 1, Model 2 and Model 3.
texts.error.renderer_failed: Supermodel's renderer could not be started: %1
texts.error.save_not_nvram: %1 is not a Supermodel NVRAM file (a <game>.nv file from Supermodel's NVRAM folder).
texts.error.wrong_machine: %1 is a game for the %2, but the project's Machine setting names another machine. Make a new project with the Machine setting set to the %2.
texts.setting.drawingscale.about: How many times the machine's own 496x384 the picture is drawn: at 2x it is 992x768, with sharper 3D. The core draws on the processor, so each step up is slower (2x draws four times the pixels). It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.idleskip.about: When the game's processor waits in a loop for something to happen, Supermodel skips ahead instead of running every pass of the loop, as upstream does by default. It makes the core faster. The game is meant to come out the same either way, but the processor spends its time differently. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which Sega arcade board the game is for: the Model 1, the Model 2 or the Model 3. A game runs only on its own board, so choose the one the game's ROM set is for. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.starttime.about: The date and time the Model 3's real-time clock shows when the machine is switched on, in UTC; it then runs with the frames (57.524 a second, as the hardware's). The default is the first of January 2000. This is a setting, and not your computer's clock, so that a movie plays back the same on any day. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.transparency.about: How the Model 1 and the Model 2 draw translucent polygons. Original: every other pixel, a checkerboard, as the hardware does. Moire: the same checkerboard on the original 496x384 grid, scaled with the Drawing Scale. Blend: half of each colour. It changes the picture only.
texts.slot.game.help: The game's ROM set: the .zip named as Supermodel and MAME name it (for example vf3.zip, scud.zip or srally2.zip). Supermodel knows a game's files by their contents, so the names of the files inside do not matter.
texts.slot.parent.help: Only for a clone (a version of a game whose set holds only the files that differ, such as vf3a.zip): the zip of the set it is a version of (vf3.zip for vf3a.zip). A game that is not a clone needs nothing here.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the game remembers, as Supermodel keeps it for each game: its NVRAM file (the EEPROM and the backup RAM, which hold the game's settings, its records and its bookkeeping), as Supermodel writes it to its NVRAM folder or as Emulator > Export Save Data wrote it (<game>.nv). It is put in the machine before the game starts. With none, the game starts with blank memory, as a new board does.
